messages.content: 你能計算從地球到一個新發現的距離為4.22光年的外行星，再到另一個距離第一顆外行星6.1光年的外行星，最後再回到距離第二顆外行星5.88光年的地球所需的時間嗎？假設真空中光的速度為299792458公尺/秒。

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning: We need to calculate light travel time for each leg: Earth to first exoplanet (4.22 ly), then first to second exoplanet (6.1 ly), then second to Earth (5.88 ly). Sum times. Use function light_travel_time. Provide results. Probably need to convert light years to meters? The function expects distance in light years and speed of light. It will compute time. We'll call function three times. Then sum. Provide answer in seconds, maybe also in years. Let's do calculations: 1 light year = distance light travels in one year. So time in years equals distance in light years. But speed given in m/s, so function will compute time in seconds. Let's compute: 4.22 ly -> 4.22 years. 6.1 ly -> 6.1 years. 5.88 ly -> 5.88 years. Total 16.2 years. In seconds: 1 year ~ 31557600 seconds (Julian year). 16.2 * 31557600 = 16.2 * 31,557,600 = 511,? Let's compute: 31,557,600 * 10 = 315,576,000; *6 = 189,345,600; *0.2 = 6,311,520. Sum = 511,? 315,576,000+189,345,600=504,921,600; +6,311,520=511,233,120 seconds. So about 5.112e8 seconds. Let's call function.
